title: Leray spectral sequence
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\mathcal F$ a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. There is a spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=\mathrm H^p\bigl(Y,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm H^{p+q}(X,\mathcal F).
$$

(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.13.4, Tag
[01F2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F2).*)

proof.text: Set D to RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f and G to RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y followed by forgetting scalars. Mathlib infers additivity and finite-limit preservation from pushforward and evaluation. For an injective I, use module_pushforward_injective_acyclic at the top open. The private proved helper derived_forget_iso compares derived G with the scalar-forgotten moduleCohomology, via InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj on a common resolution and ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for the exact forgetful functor. Transport the cohomology vanishing through this isomorphism to prove D.IsAcyclicComposablePair G.

Apply the existing source-library Functor.exists_grothendieckSpectralSequence to D, G and F. It gives the required natural-number sequence, derived second page and derived-composite abutment. This objectwise interface is recorded in src-grothendieck-spectral-sequence-nat; no Cartan–Eilenberg comparison or edge maps are used. Compose each second-page isomorphism with derived_forget_iso to identify it with the scalar-forgotten module cohomology in the statement.

D followed by scalar-forgotten global sections on Y is definitionally the scalar-forgotten global-sections functor on X (inverse image of the top open is definitionally top). Use Iso.refl for this functor isomorphism and NatTrans.rightDerived on its two directions; NatTrans.rightDerived_comp and rightDerived_id prove the inverse identities. Compose its component in degree n with derived_forget_iso for X. Apply SpectralSequence.AbutsTo.of_nonempty_iso to transport the abutment. The declared cohomology functors are exactly the right derived global sections of pqf-def-cohomology; no hypotheses or definitions change.
